title: Carnival in her youth
summary: Carnival then was much like now but with more masks; where she watched parades; whether people drank and fought more.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Let me think now, what was carnival like in those days when you were young?
I think carnival was the same as it is today. Pretty much the same. Yeah, only we had more masks, more people masks than they do now.
They dress like they do today?
Yeah, dress all different characters. I have a whole book on them. I got scrapbooks on carnival. I cut out all the clippings and put them in my scrapbook.
Where did you used to go to watch parades?

I used to go right on St. Joel Avenue, right out here. Tried to get to Canal Street to be so proud. It was just later I've been going to Canal Street to see it. But I entered the French Quarter. As I found on Royal Street, I could see it without being trampled under, you know? I don't know.
Does it say the carnival was more wild than it is now?
Is it more drinking and carrying on now?
No, I don't think. I don't think they drink any more than they do now. Looks to me as if they drink more now than they did then.
Fight more now than they did then?
Yes, they fight more now than they did then. Boy, people were more peaceful then.
They wouldn't fight at dances in those days or anything like that?
Well, I imagine they did. I didn't go to too many dances to say that. But, um...
